workload: Univariate series, T=1200, four mean regimes (0, 2, -1, 1.5) plus standard normal noise, seed 0. const_prior p=1/1201, offline StudentT, device cpu, one torch thread. The script discards one warmup call and prints the next call's milliseconds.
notes: About 73% of this call is torch.logsumexp inside the changepoint-table loop (roughly 190 rows, then the exp(-1000) cutoff). Each row materializes B[j:, j:] + head and reduces it, including the structural -inf lower triangle. Fusing that add and reduction is a local change that can leave Q, P, and Pcp identical: a dynamically compiled logsumexp matched eager values bit for bit on a random upper-triangular block and cut a 180-row loop from about 140ms to about 34ms. The scalar prior loop is real but small beside this. Finite Pcp entries are pinned to rtol 1e-12 and atol 1e-9 in tests/test_offline_changepoint_table.py. baseline_noise_pct is (max-min)/median over 7 fresh processes. Skipped online StudentT.pdf/update_theta and online_changepoint_detection, already changed in dexhunter PRs 113 and 114.

workload: Multivariate series, T=480, D=12, the same four regimes along one random unit direction, seed 0. offline_changepoint_detection with const_prior p=1/481 and FullCovarianceLikelihood, device cpu, one torch thread. The script discards one warmup call and prints the next call's milliseconds.
notes: The target is FullCovarianceLikelihood._log_marginal (this file also defines _log_marginal on StudentT, IndependentFeaturesLikelihood, and MultivariateT). It is called once per segment start from pdf_rows and is about 65% of this timing; the driver's Pcp logsumexp is under a fifth. Each call launches a chain of small float64 kernels (flat variance, scatter, Cholesky, triangular solve, two multivariate gammas). Compiling this method, leaving the bool((info != 0).any()) branch in _logdet_plus_rank_one eager, cut an n=280, d=5 detection from about 102ms to about 83ms with max abs error 1e-12 on Q, P, and Pcp, inside the relative tolerance of tests/test_offline_large_offsets.py. Keep the rank-one determinant lemma; the large-offset tests depend on it. baseline_noise_pct is (max-min)/median over 7 fresh processes.

workload: Univariate series, T=3500, four mean regimes plus standard normal noise, seed 0, passed as float32. viterbi_changepoints with constant_hazard(200) and a fresh online StudentT(alpha=0.1, beta=0.01, kappa=1, mu=0), device cpu, one torch thread. The script prints VmHWM after the call minus VmRSS just before it, in bytes. No full-size warmup: the high-water mark is monotonic.
notes: V and backpointers are both (T+1) by (T+1), float32 scores and int64 predecessors: 12*(3501)^2 = 147084012 bytes, about 94% of this peak. The recursion only reads the previous column of V, and backpointers[r, t] for r>0 is always r-1; only the changepoint predecessor backpointers[0, t] is information. Two length-(T+1) score buffers and one int64 predecessor vector leave path and changepoints identical (test_viterbi.py checks the path against an exhaustive MAP segmentation) and drop the tables from O(T^2) to O(T). Online StudentT state is O(T) and is not this peak. baseline_noise_pct is (max-min)/median over 7 fresh processes.
